title: Same Heel Again
subject: a woman who runs a one-person shoe repair kiosk in Lewisham and realises the man who brings in the same brown brogue with a worn heel every second week has been walking it down on purpose
caption: UK lovers rock, late-1970s London reggae ballad style. One-drop reggae drums with soft rimshots, deep round bass guitar, offbeat skank guitar, warm Rhodes electric piano chords. Warm analogue studio sound with light spring reverb. Female soprano, clearly sung melody, smooth and sweet with soft harmony vocals. Clear full voice, every word enunciated, steady sung melody on every line. 76 BPM, F major. Tender, shy, romantic. No dancehall, no trap drums, no autotune, no rap, no EDM synths.
lyrics:
[Intro - Rhodes, bass line]

[Verse 1]
Little kiosk by the station
Glue and polish, one small stool
Every second Monday morning
You come in with the same left shoe

[Pre-Chorus]
Brown brogue, the heel worn thin
You smile and say it's how you walk

[Chorus]
Same heel again, same heel again
Nobody wears a shoe that fast
Same heel again, I fix it then
I hope you wear it out at last

[Verse 2]
I keep your ticket by the till
I know your number off by heart
You stand and talk while the glue dries
And never look at what I charge

[Pre-Chorus]
Today you brought the right shoe too
And asked me what I do at six

[Chorus]
Same heel again, same heel again
So that's why you scuff it so
Same heel again, it's six, and then
I'll lock the shutter and we'll go

[Outro - skank guitar, Rhodes]
Same heel again, walk me home
